assessment.nobel_worthiness: The framework linking firm heterogeneity, selection, and trade gains has fundamentally reshaped modern trade research and applied policy analysis.
assessment.attribution: Melitz supplies the central heterogeneous-firm mechanism; Helpman and Redding made major complementary theoretical and empirical contributions.
assessment.maturity: Its influence, extensions, and empirical use are extensive and well established.
uncertainties: The contribution spans a large literature, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied a durable solution to pervasive identification problems in applied microeconometrics.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are central to the foundational estimator, while Blundell's work with Bond materially broadened its performance and applicability.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been tested, taught, and used across economics for decades.
uncertainties: Routine use has sometimes exceeded careful attention to finite-sample and instrument-proliferation problems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research transformed understanding of how technology and trade reallocate tasks, employment, and wages across places and workers.
assessment.attribution: Autor is central to task-based analysis, and Dorn and Hanson made pivotal joint contributions to measuring localized trade-shock consequences.
assessment.maturity: The core findings have generated a large subsequent literature and remain highly consequential for labour and trade policy.
uncertainties: The relative weight of trade, technology, and other coincident local shocks remains an active empirical question.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework made firm-level distortions a central quantitative explanation for productivity and income differences.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh and Klenow established the influential measurement approach; Restuccia has been essential in developing the broader cross-country quantitative literature.
assessment.maturity: The approach is deeply embedded in growth and development research and has stimulated extensive measurement and policy work.
uncertainties: Measured wedges need not map one-to-one into policy-remediable distortions or causal barriers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Collateral constraints and amplification mechanisms gave macroeconomics a powerful account of credit cycles and financial propagation.
assessment.attribution: Kiyotaki and Moore provided the canonical collateral-cycle framework; Gertler made foundational complementary contributions to the financial accelerator.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have withstood repeated use in macroeconomic modeling and became especially salient after financial crises.
uncertainties: Credit-friction models are a family of mechanisms, so the boundaries of a single prize-worthy discovery are contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian trade models made welfare gains from trade measurable in disciplined, transparent general-equilibrium systems.
assessment.attribution: Kortum is foundational to the modern quantitative Ricardian tradition, with Costinot and Rodriguez-Clare making key theoretical and welfare-measurement contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a workhorse for contemporary trade analysis.
uncertainties: Estimated gains and counterfactuals remain sensitive to assumptions about adjustment, market structure, and dynamic effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on household leverage and mortgage credit materially changed accounts of consumption collapses and macroeconomic crises.
assessment.attribution: Mian and Sufi are central to the empirical and conceptual account of debt-driven downturns; Campbell made major foundational contributions to household finance and mortgage economics.
assessment.maturity: The contribution has proved influential in macro-finance and policy debates since the global financial crisis.
uncertainties: The appropriate balance between household-debt mechanisms and broader banking or monetary mechanisms differs across crises.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterogeneous-agent New Keynesian models substantially improved analysis of distributional incidence and transmission of macroeconomic policy.
assessment.attribution: Kaplan, Moll, and Violante are the clear central contributors to the modern HANK formulation represented here.
assessment.maturity: The framework is highly influential and increasingly used, though younger than several higher-ranked contributions.
uncertainties: Its empirical discipline and policy implications remain actively developed, so long-run consensus is not yet complete.
